reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address thermal pre-oxidation of Q235 steel or its corrosion behavior; E1 concerns a high-entropy alloy in molten salt at 700°C, and E2 studies laser-clad CoCrFeNiTix coatings on Q235, not pre-oxidation. No specific prior evidence supports the key premises about oxide formation, barrier properties, or corrosion suppression in the proposed system.
premises: Controlled thermal pre-oxidation of Q235 steel forms a uniform, adherent passivating oxide layer
This oxide layer suppresses corrosion in chloride-containing environments at room and elevated temperatures
The oxide layer is less defective than the native oxide and acts as a barrier to corrosive species
Pre-oxidized Q235 will show lower corrosion current density, higher corrosion potential, and reduced weight loss vs. untreated steel
